column1: Video: Automated deploy with terraform apply and Ansible (10)
column2: Video checkpoint 1: `terraform apply` output shown with new resources created, Ansible playbook run shown against the provisioned instance, and service confirmed running after the playbook completes.
column6: All three elements clearly shown: terraform apply output, Ansible playbook run, and service confirmed running.
column9: Two of three elements shown, or one is ambiguous (e.g., Ansible run not shown against the Terraform-provisioned instance, or service health not confirmed after playbook).
column12: No credible automated deploy sequence demonstrated.

column1: Video: Service reachability after automated deploy (10)
column2: Video checkpoint 2: `nmap -sV -Pn -p T:25565 <public-endpoint>` output shows port open with Minecraft service responding and MOTD containing name or student ID, run against the Terraform/Ansible-provisioned service.
column6: nmap output clearly shows 25565/tcp open with Minecraft service and MOTD containing name or student ID, run against the automated-deploy service.
column9: Reachability shown but MOTD is missing name/ID, nmap output is incomplete, or it is unclear whether the service was provisioned by Terraform/Ansible or manually.

column2: Video checkpoint 3: GitHub Actions run tab or screenshot clearly shows a successful pipeline run triggered by a tag push, with image acquisition/build, smoke test, and image push steps visible.
column6: Successful Actions run clearly shown with tag trigger, image acquisition/build, smoke test, and push steps all visible.
column9: Pipeline success evidenced but one step is not visible or unclear (e.g., smoke test not distinct, tag trigger not confirmed, image acquisition/build is not visible, or push not shown).
column12: No credible CI/CD pipeline success evidence provided.

column2: Video checkpoint 4: `terraform destroy` shown removing resources, followed by `terraform apply` and Ansible playbook run, with the server confirmed joinable (e.g., nmap) after rebuild and the restoration outcome made clear (same world restored or fresh world created).
column6: Full destroy, apply, and Ansible run shown in sequence; server confirmed joinable after rebuild; restoration outcome is clearly explained or evidenced.
column9: Destroy and rebuild attempted but one phase is unclear, server is not confirmed joinable after rebuild, or the restoration outcome is not made clear.
column12: No credible destroy and rebuild cycle demonstrated.

column2: Evaluated on four elements: (1) all required resources provisioned or cleanly referenced (networking/subnet and public entry point strategy, Security Group with TCP 25565, EC2 instance, pre-existing `LabInstanceProfile` attached), (2) `LabInstanceProfile` enables ECR pull and S3 write without hardcoded credentials on the host, (3) Security Group rules are minimal and justified at the relevant admin and public entry points, (4) input variables are named, typed, and documented.
column6: All four elements present and correctly implemented.
column9: Three of four elements present and correctly implemented; one minor gap.
column12: Two of four elements present; significant missing configuration in networking, IAM, or SG.
column15: Fewer than two elements present or Terraform code does not provision the required infrastructure.

column2: Evaluated on three elements: (1) playbook completes all required configuration steps (install prerequisites, authenticate to ECR, pull pinned image, configure persistent storage, restore world data from S3 when rebuilding/recovering, set required environment variables including `EULA=TRUE`, start service), (2) playbook is idempotent; re-running against the same host produces no errors and no unintended changes, (3) tasks are clearly named and logically ordered.
column6: All three elements present; playbook is complete, idempotent, and clearly structured.
column9: Two of three elements present; one area has meaningful gaps (e.g., a step is missing, idempotency not confirmed, or task ordering is unclear).
column12: Only one element clearly present; significant manual intervention still required to reach a running service.
column15: No Ansible playbook provided or playbook does not produce a working service.

column2: Evaluated on three elements: (1) GitHub Actions workflow triggers on a git tag push, (2) workflow acquires or builds the deployable image, smoke-tests it, and publishes it to ECR, (3) at least one successful pipeline run is clearly evidenced (link to Actions tab or screenshot showing green run with all steps).
column6: All three elements present and correctly implemented.
column9: Two of three elements present; one is missing or weak (e.g., smoke test is trivial, trigger is on push not tag, publish step missing, or evidence of successful run is ambiguous).
column12: Only one element clearly present; pipeline does not reliably publish a tested image to ECR.
column15: No CI/CD pipeline provided or pipeline does not publish images to ECR.

column2: All four required documentation sections present and usable (architecture diagram showing AWS resources + Ansible flow + CI/CD pipeline, Terraform variable documentation, change process for infrastructure changes, teardown checklist to prevent runaway cost), and world data recovery strategy documented and defensible.
column6: All five items (four doc sections + world data strategy) present, accurate, and usable by another operator without asking clarifying questions.
column9: Four of five items complete or one section has a minor gap; overall usable by a new operator.
column12: Three of five items complete or multiple sections are too vague to act on; teardown checklist or world data strategy missing.
column15: Fewer than three items present or documentation is not usable by another operator.
